title: Programming languages
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Understand how programming languages work and differ: paradigms, syntax, tokenizing and parsing, abstract syntax trees and interpreters, environments and scope, first-class functions and closures, functional programming, types and type checking, objects and dynamic dispatch, and memory management; build an interpreter for a small language.

weeks.3: Abstract syntax trees and recursive-descent parsing
weeks.7: Functional programming: map, filter, reduce and recursion
weeks.9: Types: static and dynamic, strong and weak

blocks.deliverable: Write a tokenizer for arithmetic expressions.
Write a parser and evaluator for arithmetic.
Add variables and functions to the interpreter.
Week 7 midterm; rewrite loops as functional code.
Write a type checker for a tiny language.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Build a complete interpreter in Python for a small language (your own design or the supplied one) with numbers, booleans, variables, if expressions, and functions with closures and recursion, plus a test suite of 30 programs and a written language reference.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
